We have mass spec: m/z 224.120115... likely molecular ion M+? The formula from candidate SMILES C16H16O has exact mass: C16=16*12.0000=192, H16=16*1.007825=16.1252, O=15.9949 total =224.1201 matches. So formula C16H16O fits mass. Carbon NMR shows many aromatic carbons: many around 128-129, plus carbonyl ~196.8, plus aliphatic ~37.5,36.39,26.41. So structure likely a phenyl ketone with a propyl chain attached to aromatic. The SMILES we guessed: CCCc1ccc(cc1)C(=O)c2ccccc2. That is 1-phenyl-3-phenylpropanone? Actually it's 1-phenyl-3-phenylpropan-1-one? Let's check: propyl attached to phenyl ring, carbonyl attached to second phenyl. So overall C16H16O matches. Carbon NMR: carbonyl at 196.8 matches. Aromatic carbons: two phenyl rings give many signals. Aliphatic: propyl chain: CH2-CH2-CH3 attached to aromatic: chemical shifts ~37.5 (benzylic CH2), 36.39 (next CH2), 26.41 (CH3). That fits. So likely correct.

We should validate SMILES with validate tool.
